name: Ramada Encore by Wyndham Busan Station
detail: This is the hotel I chose for a 2-night, 3-day trip to Busan with my daughter. The front desk staff were very kind (thank you for the hotel room upgrade), and the room was clean, making our stay comfortable. Above all, it's only a 2-minute walk from Busan Station and the Busan subway station, and Starbucks is in the same building, so the location is excellent 👍 If I come to Busan again, I will definitely choose this place^^

name: Centum Business Hotel
detail: The hotel front desk speaks Chinese and also provides breakfast from the Mama Buffet on the third floor! It's only a bit over 200 for one night, where can you find such a good deal? It's perfect for one person, but may be a bit cramped for two. The room is overall quite tidy, and it's about a 300-meter walk from Centum City subway station, exit 11. It's within walking distance to Shinsegae Department Store, and there's a GS25 convenience store downstairs. I will choose this place again when I come to Busan next time.

name: Signiel Busan
detail: My first trip to Busan. I chose to stay by the sea. The room has a great view of the ocean, which is fantastic. The lounge had champagne, and I had a good time. The Sky Capsule station was also nearby and very convenient. I want to stay here again.

name: Toyoko Inn Busan Seomyeon
detail: I've stayed at the Toyoko Inn in Somyon for the first time, and I was surprised by the various services, including the free ones. There is a Wowpass machine in the lobby. Free pajamas, an ice maker, a water server, and a coin laundry were extremely helpful. The room has a toilet with a washlet and a bathtub. In the morning, there is a free breakfast. Although the selection is small, the menu changes slightly every day, and since it's a buffet, you can eat as much as you want. You can also drink free coffee until 10:30 in the morning. It's within walking distance not only from Seomyeon Station but also from Bujeon Station. It was convenient.

name: Toyoko Inn Busan Station 1
detail: I used this hotel for my first solo trip to Busan. This time, I went sightseeing in Seoul by train from Busan, and since my return train was expected to arrive after midnight, its proximity to the station—so close that I could call it directly connected—and the bright surroundings were truly reassuring. There are various shops inside Busan Station. There are also many convenience stores and restaurants around the hotel, with a Dunkin' Donuts right next door, making it very convenient. The ability to store my luggage in the lobby lockers before check-in and after check-out was also helpful. Additionally, since there’s a taxi stand right in front of the hotel, moving back to the airport was smooth, and everything remained stress-free until the end. The room had a large bed that was super comfortable. The air conditioning worked well, and the lighting was bright and comfortable. The spacious refrigerator was also convenient. The amenities included one bottle of water, one large and one small towel, non-disposable slippers, body soap, and shampoo & conditioner. There wasn't a closet, but there were hangers, so I was able to hang my clothes. The staff spoke Japanese, which helped me feel secure during my first solo trip. At the breakfast buffet, the porridge and oden were particularly delicious, and there was a variety of bread and drinks. Even for someone like me who isn't fond of spicy food, there were plenty of non-spicy options, so I was able to enjoy a proper meal every morning. I am completely satisfied with the location, sense of安心, comfort, and service. I definitely want to stay here again when I visit Busan!

name: Avenue Haeundae by The solid residence
detail: I stayed for 4 nights on my first solo trip to Busan. Perhaps because I wrote in the request section that I would like to spend quietly if possible, they made an effort to prepare a corner room for me, and fortunately, the neighbors were also quiet (I couldn't tell if they were there or not), and I had a good night's sleep at night. Even at local Japanese hotels, it can be difficult to fall asleep due to the environment or noise depending on the room, but I was able to sleep well abroad, which was a great help. Many reviews mentioned that there are only two elevators, so they take a while to come, but I didn't feel that way. Of course, being elevators, there was some waiting, but it didn't bother me at all; rather, I felt it was smoother to come and go than I had imagined. The location was great, as I could see the sea from the window of my room, and it was just a short walk to the beach. There are Korean convenience stores and a 7-Eleven nearby, and on the main street, there are Daiso and Art Box, as well as Haeundae Station, so I think it’s very convenient. In fact, I forgot to bring a sponge to wash my body, and I was able to quickly rush to the nearby Daiso, which was a lifesaver (laughs). As for amenities, there was a microwave, kettle, and drum-type washing machine in the room, so I managed with those. Since the kettle and washing machine are likely used by various tourists, I think it's a good idea to thoroughly sanitize them with boiling water and clean the washing tub before using them. There were three 500ml bottles of water in the refrigerator provided for free, which was helpful on the first day. Also, the pump-type item in the bathroom is toothpaste that is popular in Korea, so please make sure not to confuse it with hand soap. (There is also a new mini soap provided.) On the evening of the second day, when I accidentally left the card key inside the room despite it being auto-lock, I was able to call the hotel reception on the second floor, and they came immediately to assist me. (Please note that it is basically self-check-in and self-check-out.) I reserved a month before Silver Week, and I was able to stay at a very reasonable and incredible price and was shown a really nice room, so I am truly, truly, very satisfied. If I have the opportunity to visit Haeundae again, I would like to use this place or recommend it to friends. Thank you very much!

name: Urbanstay Seomyeon
detail: It’s in the city center. Access is good wherever you’re heading. Close to two stations. It’s not too far from either the airport or the shore. Our room was larger and cleaner than we’d expected. Multiple lifts are available. You can enjoy views of the hills from the rooftop. Housekeeping staff were friendly and nice.

name: Toyoko Inn Busan Jungang Station
detail: The distance from Busan Station is walkable in this weather, the luggage storage service is good, it's easy to get a ride since it's by the roadside, breakfast is good, the bedding is clean, hot water comes out well, drainage works well, and there was no smell of cigarette smoke, which was nice. Although there is distance, I plan to stay again. It's great for solo travel.

name: Stanford hotel Busan
detail: I booked individual rooms for a group trip with friends. The location was just a 2-minute walk from Jagalchi Station, close to BIFF Square, and Oryang was also very accessible just across the crosswalk, making it a great spot. My room was on the 10th floor, and it was spacious and comfortable for one person, with a bathtub that allowed me to relax while watching TV. The daily cleaning was thorough as well. However, there was an issue with the toilet from the start, as it didn't flush well, and despite being careful, on the morning of the third day, the toilet clogged, and water overflowed, which was surprising. But when I contacted the front desk, a staff member with a plunger quickly came to my room and resolved the clog. On the day of our return, there were four adults with four large suitcases and four small ones, but the front desk arranged for a jumbo taxi, and we could get to the airport for 50,000₩. The staff at the front desk was very kind and helpful, so I thought I would like to use this hotel again if I have the chance.

name: NOMADX Stay Hostel
detail: This time I chose a single room, and there are a lot of compartments in the room for placing items. Each room has an independent password lock, so even if you go out, the power won't cut off. The capsule dormitory also has individual doors with password locks for each compartment, and I feel that the soundproofing won't be too bad. There are about six restrooms and six shower rooms for females, all very clean. I also didn't encounter any waiting situations. The common lounge area is very spacious; you can choose to work alone here or meet some friends from other places. A simple breakfast in a European and American style is provided from 8 to 10 in the morning, including bread slices, cereal, and coffee. The staff here comes from all over the world, and many are traveling while working. They are always willing to help. Overall, it was a very satisfying accommodation experience, and if I travel to Busan alone again next time, I would still consider staying here!
